claim: For every nondecreasing locally finite infinite sequence (a_i) of positive integers with bounded numerical multiplicity, if every tail has gcd one and its finite subset sums meet every residue class modulo every positive integer, liminf_{X->infinity} (log 2)#{i:a_i<=X}/log X>1, sum_i ||alpha a_i||^2=infinity for every irrational real alpha (where ||x|| is distance to the nearest integer), and (S_m-a_{m+1})/a_{m+1}^beta tends to positive infinity for every real beta with 0<beta<1, where S_m=sum_{i=1}^m a_i, then there exist integers L>=0 and m_0>=1 such that for every m>=m_0, S_m>=2L and every integer in [L,S_m-L] is a subset sum of a_1,...,a_m using each labelled index at most once.

quadruple.statement: For every nondecreasing locally finite infinite sequence (a_i) of positive integers with bounded numerical multiplicity, if every tail has gcd one and its finite subset sums meet every residue class modulo every positive integer, liminf_{X->infinity} (log 2)#{i:a_i<=X}/log X>1, sum_i ||alpha a_i||^2=infinity for every irrational real alpha (where ||x|| is distance to the nearest integer), and (S_m-a_{m+1})/a_{m+1}^beta tends to positive infinity for every real beta with 0<beta<1, where S_m=sum_{i=1}^m a_i, then there exist integers L>=0 and m_0>=1 such that for every m>=m_0, S_m>=2L and every integer in [L,S_m-L] is a subset sum of a_1,...,a_m using each labelled index at most once.
quadruple.stage: Locally finite labelled sequences of positive integers, finite subset sums, modular arithmetic and real asymptotic limits.

shape.objects: Infinite countable nondecreasing integer sequences with a uniform finite multiplicity bound. Candidate sequences are determined by finite paired blocks and extended by adjoining a new pair under a fixed arithmetic recursion. The sequence, finite subsets, powers, floors and real limits have standard classical and Lean/Mathlib definitions. No rigidity theorem, continuous parameter, random ensemble or spread family is recorded.
shape.quantifiers: For every such sequence, assume one finite bound on value multiplicity, the stated arithmetic conditions for every tail and modulus, the strict liminf counting condition, irrational norm divergence for every irrational alpha, and surplus divergence relative to every fixed exponent beta in (0,1); then there exist fixed L and m_0 giving central-prefix coverage for every m>=m_0. The leading quantifier is universal, so one fully verified sequence failing the conclusion refutes the inference.
shape.target_quantity: A yes/no sufficiency decision, not an extremal numerical optimum. A finite constant L would suffice for the conclusion. The negative alternative requires an infinite counterexample, not a finite prefix.
shape.ambient_structure: Additive order and arithmetic coexist. Adjoining successive paired blocks supplies a recursive extension operation. The candidate affine relation between adjacent blocks has constant one, while a digit-coefficient encoding is intended to control support. No measurable random ensemble, dependence statistic, transform bias, or category transport is recorded.
shape.symmetries: Swapping equal-value labels preserves the property. An arbitrary translation or dilation need not preserve the arithmetic hypotheses. No system of structured pieces with a proved intersection or transport closure is recorded.
shape.configuration: The required relation is eventual coverage of every integer in every central prefix interval with one fixed endpoint loss. The candidate extension must preserve order, two labelled copies per level, the affine pair relation, a digit-coefficient support bound, and quantitative surplus inequalities. Finite truncation does not itself certify the infinite configuration.
shape.extremal_candidate: A specific nonextremal paired floor-perturbation template is recorded in the strategy study. It is not yet a proved counterexample or an optimising family; no rigidity or optimum is asserted.
shape.finite_certificates: A finite seed can be evaluated by hand after proving the extension law. The smallest nontrivial paired-block parameter is one pair, starting at level j=2, and positivity of its surplus can be checked there. Finite subset-sum questions are computable but no finite prefix certifies the full infinite claim and no mathematical computation is admitted.
shape.monotonicity: Central coverage of a fixed prefix becomes weaker as L increases within its valid range. Neither the entire conjunction nor the extension's all-future conclusion has a proved finite stopping threshold; no distinguished smallest open L is recorded.
shape.uniformity_parameter: Every infinite sequence with the stated properties, every tail and modulus, every irrational alpha, and each fixed beta in (0,1). The asymptotic threshold may depend on beta; no uniformity as beta approaches one is requested.
shape.proof_shape: A complete computer-free counterexample proof is written in moves/001-paired-perturbation.md. The paired extension laws precede the analytical seed. They give all-prefix surplus growth for every fixed beta, every-tail gcd and modular coverage, irrational norm divergence, strict label counting, and a base-three coefficient bound leaving at least X-floor(X/9) missing integers in [1,X]. Independent result review remains due.
shape.neighbours: The earlier constant-perturbation generic inference is known false in the local predecessor proof, but that sequence has only logarithmic endpoint surplus and fails the present stronger antecedent. Qualitative surplus for actual admissible pure-power streams is accepted at checkpoint-000009. The exact current inference, its pure-power quantitative profile, C1 and the original root remain open. Burr-Erdos DOI 10.1016/0022-314X(81)90036-6 gives perturbed-sequence obstructions and a completeness lemma with disjoint supplies; neither is a verbatim model or equivalence for this conjunction. Finite prefixes of the old and new templates are computable, without execution permission.
shape.known_bounds: The recorded old translated-power construction has sparse numerical subset-sum support despite label abundance and arithmetic non-obstruction, but its logarithmic surplus stops short of the new all-sublinear-power hypothesis. The strategy study compresses a prospective counterexample into a specific paired floor-perturbation template and extension, not a certified result. No finite tail residue, first moment, established common-method barrier, target-equivalence theorem, or explicit conditional threshold is recorded. Move 1 proves the exact candidate counting exponent log 4/log 3 and the numerical support bound #FS intersect [1,X]<=floor(X/9), together with surplus at least an exponential divided by a quadratic polynomial in the level. These are analytical candidate results pending independent acceptance, not finite experiments.
shape.missing_input: No mathematical input remains unproved in the exact counterexample candidate; independent result review remains due. This decides only the abstract inference, not the separate pure-power profile, C1 or the original root.
shape.base_theory: ZFC and ordinary countable classical number theory. The recursive construction and any elementary arithmetic checks remain inside this theory, whose foundations Lean's standard classical axioms cover. No uncountable threshold, guessing principle, independence claim or extra axiom is available or needed.
